correctness.rationale: For every finite tree, direct counting under one uniform leaf split gives exact increments of cherry count, total tip depth and cherry-tip depth sum. Multiplying increments before averaging yields the mixed moment recurrence. Induction from n=3 establishes the first-moment identities and K_(n+1)=(n-1)K_n/n-2/9, whence global K_n=-(n-3)(n+2)/(9(n-1)); uniform tip sampling gives local covariance 2/9 and conditional depth gap 1. Boundaries n=2 and n=3 specified. A standalone standard-library exact verifier passed 60,677 assertions across 46,233 growth histories and 873 independent transition cases; finite checks are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact two-scale sign reversal was compared by implication with the Yule cherry marginal law, the Sackin first moment, Yule cherry/pitchfork joint distribution, Sackin/cophenetic joint analysis, and outbreak-tree correlations. Neither marginal first moments nor the different joint distributions imply the new mixed moment; independent all-size transition identities supply it. Semantic searches of published mathematical research records returned no equivalent statement. Historical priority remains uncertain, especially unindexed multivariate tree enumerations and inaccessible dissertation material.

value.rationale: Cherry count and Sackin topological depth are widely used and motivated phylogenetic shape/imbalance observables. The exact sign reversal separates sampled-tip association (cherry tips one edge deeper on average) from whole-tree negative covariance for every n>=4. This is a structural phenomenon with a complete closed-form dependence baseline, not a marginal cherry or Sackin calculation, and the two-scale distinction matters when interpreting shape measures. No downstream inference performance theorem or independent priority certification is claimed.
